messages:
maria: Hey team — customer 54F reported a spike in 5xxs (502/504) to hosted API since ~08:10 UTC. They see TLS handshake timeouts from our gateway. Can someone pick this up?

sam: on it. do we have a quick repro or a request id from the customer?

maria: they provided a curl sample: `curl -v https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer <redacted>\" --max-time 10` — it intermittently times out during TLS. sometimes returns HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway.

devon: any recent cert rotations or edge changes pushed in that timeframe?

maria: Ops console shows cert rotation started at 08:05 UTC and completed at 08:12 UTC, but the certificate chain appears fine in a cursory check. stack traces show repeated `SSL_connect: ssl handshake failure` in gateway logs.

ops-bot: [ALERT] 08:11:22 gateway-edge-03: 502 surge (rate 14/min) — ops-runbook triggered.

lee: request logs (gateway) for that customer id please — need gateway->upstream handshake timings.

maria: attaching redacted excerpt from gateway log (timestamps aligned):

```
08:10:58 gateway-edge-03 client=10.2.3.4 req_id=abc123 upstream=upstream-api-1 ssl_connect_start
08:11:00 gateway-edge-03 client=10.2.3.4 req_id=abc123 upstream=upstream-api-1 ssl_connect_timeout 10000ms
08:11:00 gateway-edge-03 client=10.2.3.4 req_id=abc123 returned 502 to client
08:11:05 gateway-edge-03 client=10.2.3.4 req_id=def456 upstream=upstream-api-2 ssl_connect_start
08:11:07 gateway-edge-03 client=10.2.3.4 req_id=def456 ssl_connect_error: tlsv1 alert protocol version
```

sam: hmm `ssl_connect_timeout` + `tlsv1 alert protocol version` in same window. Could be resolver returning truncated/misleading answers causing fallback to TCP and delaying handshake?

devon: can someone run a quick DNS check from the edge host that served the failing reqs? `dig` + `openssl s_client` from that node.

lee: ran on edge-03 (08:13 UTC):
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.com @our-resolver
; <<>> DiG 9.10.6 <<>> +short api.redwood.com @10.11.12.13
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
Then tried public resolver:
```
$ dig +short api.redwood.com @1.1.1.1
93.184.216.34
```
And tcpdump shows a lot of UDP retransmits to 10.11.12.13 and several responses with TC (truncated) flags.
```
08:12:59 IP edge-03.12345 > 10.11.12.13.53: UDP, length 68
08:13:00 IP 10.11.12.13.53 > edge-03.12345: UDP, length 512 (TC set)
08:13:00 IP edge-03.12345 > 10.11.12.13.53: UDP, length 68
08:13:02 IP edge-03.12345 > 10.11.12.13.53: UDP, length 68 (retransmit)
```

maria: customer says this started during cert rotation window. could be two issues colliding: cert rotation causing slight increase in handshake work + resolver unhealthy causing queries to stall -> handshake timeouts.

sam: agree. quick mitigation ideas: 1) temporarily route edge hosts to alternate DNS (1.1.1.1/8.8.8.8) 2) increase upstream TLS handshake timeout slightly (safe short term) 3) throttle cert reload concurrency.

devon: pushed DNS fallback to 1.1.1.1 on edge-03 and edge-04 at 08:20 UTC. after change, `dig` responded immediately and curl repros improved — reduced 502s for that customer.

ops-bot: [RUNBOOK] applied dns-fallback profile to edge-03,04 by devon at 08:20:12 UTC.

lee: also captured an `openssl s_client` attempt against upstream during failure window:
```
$ openssl s_client -connect upstream-api-1.redwood:443 -servername api.redwood.com -timeout 5
CONNECTED(00000003)
140736...:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:tlsv1 alert protocol version:SSL alert number 70
---
no peer certificate available
---
```

maria: that alert matched some log entries. curious that some attempts show `protocol version` instead of `timeout` — likely because TCP fallback for large DNS resulted in extra latency and some older clients attempted legacy ciphers? (less likely).

sam: primary takeaway: DNS path was flaky (UDP truncation -> retries -> TCP -> delay) during a period of high cert reload activity. The combination pushed some edge handshakes past configured timeouts and produced 502s.

devon: immediate remedy (done): dns fallback + rollback cert reload concurrency to single-host-at-a-time. medium-term: enable EDNS buffer size tuning and ensure recursive resolvers advertise proper TCP fallback. Also add healthcheck on resolver that checks for TC responses and switches provider automatically.

maria: customer rollback note: we asked customer to retry and provided temporary workaround of using `--resolve api.redwood.com:443:93.184.216.34` for urgent ops. They confirmed improved success.

lee: created a dashboard tile for `gateway_tls_handshake_time` and `dns_tc_rate` and alerted on combined high percentiles. Ticket INF-3421 created for follow-up.

maria: next steps for postmortem:
- root cause hypothesis: intermittent UDP truncation + slow TCP fallback from our resolver during cert rotation traffic spike; caused handshake timeouts and protocol-alert responses as downstream connections retried and negotiated differently.
- immediate mitigations applied: DNS fallback to public resolvers, reduced cert-reload concurrency, bumped handshake timeout from 10s->12s for 1h window.
- follow-ups: automation for resolver failover, EDNS MTU tuning, update runbook to include cert-rotation throttles, notify customers about planned rotations.

sam: confirmed moving to internal postmortem. tagging infra-sre & security to review certificate reload process and rotation cadence.

ops-bot: [INFO] Customer 54F reported issue resolved at 08:45 UTC after mitigations.

maria: closing thread for now — will attach PM notes when INF-3421 is ready. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
